what_they_do: Paid customers AED 1 per minute late ('Dirhams for Delays'); drivers not penalised and cannot see the ETA
lesson_for_noon: Shows a public late-delivery guarantee works as marketing. Our Solution 1 is cheaper: credit only persuadable customers.

what_they_do: 15-minute Amazon Now from neighbourhood micro-fulfilment centres plus 2-hour delivery
lesson_for_noon: Raises customer expectations for speed, so an honest, kept promise matters even more.

what_they_do: Inspection 2–5 working days after the item reaches the warehouse; refund 7–14 business days to card
lesson_for_noon: Long, invisible waits are what Solution 2's trust tiers and refund tracker remove for low-risk customers.

what_they_do: Refunds to noon store credit within 24 hours after inspection
lesson_for_noon: noon already runs a wallet-first refund in one market, so instant wallet refunds are operationally possible.

what_they_do: Trustpilot replies ask customers to email care@noon.com with a subject line; ~97–98% of negative reviews answered
lesson_for_noon: noon replies to almost every review, but with a template. Solution 3 is about one owner and a fix, not more replies.
